english: V | Government of Ghana - 2021 Citizens’ Budget MESSAGE FROM THE MINISTER FOR FINANCE

twi: Ɔpenimma bosome mu wɔ 2020 mu no, Ghanafoɔ too aba maa Ɔmanpanin Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo bio sɛ ontoa adwuma pa a reyɛ no so na nyɛ nnepa bebree nka dees reyɛ no ho.
english: The good people of Ghana in December 2020 voted to retain H.E. the President, Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo for another term to continue the good work and do more.

twi: Ɛnyɛ ades a ystoto awerehyem a Ghanafoɔ anya wɔ saa aban yi mu no ase koraa.
english: The confidence reposed in this Government by our fellow Ghanaians is one we do not take for granted.

twi: 2021 Sikasɛm Nhyehysee yi yɛ Sikasɛm Nhyehyeses a ɛyɛ sononko koraa ɛsiane sɛ ebetoto yɛn Sikasɛm yie na aboa abɔ ɔmanfoɔ ho ban, ebekanyan nnwuma a wɔwɔ haw mu na afei aboa yɛn ama yɛde yɛn ahoɔden adi dwuma de ama Ghanaman asane asi ne mpontuo ɛkwan so wo ɛberɛ a COVID-19 yadeɛ kontonkurowi ano abrɛ ase yi akyi. Saa Sikasɛm Nhyehysee yi gyina yɛn anisoadehunu sɛ yɛpɛ sɛ yesesa Ɔman yi na ɛyɛ Ɔman a ɛde ne ho wɔ sikaskm mu no so.
english: The 2021 Budget is a landmark budget that reorganises our public finances to protect lives, revitalise troubled businesses, and consciously focus our energies on building back a better Ghana, post COVID-19. The Budget is anchored on our vision transforming this country and build a self-sustaining economy.

twi: Mfeɛ ɛnan a ɛdi kan no, yɛnam akwanhodoɔ so ayɛ nhyehysee sɛ Ɔman yi bɛsane agyina ne nan so wo Sikasɛm mu. Nhyehyses ahodos yi ne deɛ sebema nnwuma abu so, akwanhodo» a ysfa so nya sika gu ɔman Fotoɔ mu, anammɔntuo ahodoɔ a ama nnwuma atu mpon, ankorankorɛ nnwuma mu mmoa ne asetenam mpontuo ho mmoa a yɛde maa mmoborowafoo.
english: For most part of the first term, we have put the economy back on track, through a series of carefully planned programmes of macroeconomic adjustments, introduced revenue-enhancing measures, implemented growth-inducing interventions, supported the private sector, and rolled out social intervention programmes.

twi: Afe 2019 kɔɔ awiees no, na Ghanaman nam ɛkwan pa wo Sikasɛm mu mpontuo so a na nneɛma a ɛma nnwuma ne Sikasɛm tu mpɔn nyinaa di adansees, na amansan nso agye yɛn atom sɛ yɛyɛ Ɔman a yɛnam mpontuo kwan so, na ɛno mu na COVID-19 yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi bɛto hyse yɛn so.
english: By the end 2019, we were solidly on the path of economic transformation on the back of impressive macroeconomic indicators and international endorsement as a country on the rise, when we were struck by the COVID-19 pandemic.

twi: Ewiase aman a Ghana ka ho bie nyinaa anya saa yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi ho nsunsuansoɔ bɔne no bi.
english: The devastating impact of this pandemic has been felt by all economies globally, including Ghana.

twi: Covid-19 yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi de haw ahodovs absto yɛn so na ako atia yɛn nnwuma ne daadaa abrabɔ.
english: The outbreak of the Covid-19 Pandemic presented a lot of difficulties which have affected our businesses and daily livelihoods.

twi: Aban ahunu sɛdeɛ saa yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi de nsunsuansoɔ bɔne abrɛ ɔmanfoo, yei enti, aban ayɛ nhyehysee ahodovs de reboa nnwuma sɛdeɛ bɛyɛ a Yɛbɛsane asi yɛn dada mu.
english: Government, however, has noticed with great concern the effect of the pandemic on us as a people and has initiated policies to help revive businesses and bring our lives back to normalcy.

twi: Anidasoo wo ho ɛsiane sɛ yɛahunu akwan afoforɔ a yɛbɛfa so adi dwuma a ɛde akwannya bebree beba.
english: All hope is not lost because we have found new ways of doing things with endless possibilities.

twi: Aban asi nkete sɛ ɔbɛhwɛ sɛ ɔmanfoɔ bɛnya apomuden, yei enti, wayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ sɛ Ghanani biara nwo panees ntia saa yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi sedes bɛyɛ a yɛn nyinaa bɛnya apɔmuden de ayɛ adwuma de apagya Ghanaman aduru mpempensos a yɛn nyinaa hwehwɛ no.
english: Government is committed to making sure we have a healthy population and as such has arranged for Ghanaians to be vaccinated to ensure that we all stay strong to build the Ghana we wish to see.

twi: Yɛne mo aka abom ayɛ adwuma wɔ haw ahodoɔ nyinaa mu wɔ yɛn mpontuo anammɔn a yɛnam so yi mu, na yɛde akokoɔduru atu anammoɔn ahodoɔ sedes ɛbɛyɛ a yɛde Ɔman yi Sikasɛm bɛsane asi kankorɔ ɛkwan so.
english: We have partnered with you even in the midst of difficulties as part of our development process and have taken bold steps to put our economy back on track to development.

twi: Seesei, Ghanafoɔ bɛyɛ ɔpepem baako ne ahanu (1.2 million) na wɔanya akwannya ko Ntoasoɔ Sukuu a sbesesa wɔn abrabo, yɛasane asiesie tebea a na ɛnyɛ wɔ sikakorabea nnwuma mu nyinaa na nnipa dodov no ara nsa aka wɔn sika a na akɔdi sikakorabea nnwuma a na aguo no nyinaa mu.
english: About 1.2 million Ghanaians can now have a better and quality secondary education for life, we have cleaned up the banking sector and most customers have received their savings from the collapsed banks.

twi: Bio, yegasi adwumakuo a ehyehye ahyɛn wɔ yɛn ɔman yi mu na ysahunu ahyɛn a adwumakuo yi adi kan ayɛ wo ahyenton edwa ahodov ne yɛn akwan so.
english: Additionally, a vehicle assembling plant has been built and we have seen the first batch of assembled vehicles on our market and roads.

twi: Nokwasem ne se, yɛgye tom sɛ yesahyia ɔhaw ahodoɔ wo ɛberɛ a yɛgu so rebɔ mmoɔden atu yɛn mpontuo botaeɛ ahodoɔ ho anammɔn no.
english: We honestly admit that we faced some challenges as we tried to promote our development goals.

twi: Aban ani abere pa ara reyɛ nhyehyesee ahodoɔ de ape saa haw ahodoɔ yi nnannuaguberɛ sedes bye a ɛde ahoto bebre nnwumakuo.
english: Government is earnestly putting measures in place to solve these problems and bring relief to businesses.

twi: Ebi ne se, bosome Kotonimma mu wo afe 2020 mu no, yɛde Ghana sika sidi oọpepem ahanson ne aduonum (GH¢750 million) boaa nnwuma nketewa, adantam ne akesee2 ne afoforɔ bi wo dwumadie a yɛato edin sɛ “CAP-BuSS” Dwumadie no mu.
english: For instance, we rolled-out the GH¢750 million CAP-BuSS Programme in May 2020 and this has provided support to Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (MSMEs) and many others.

twi: Seesei dee, ɛho akɔhia pa ara sene ɛberɛ a abɛsene koro no sɛ yesoso yɛn nsa na yeka bom toa so tu akokoɔduru anammɔn ahodov a bɛma yɛn nsa aka mpontuo a yɛrepɛ ama yɛn ho no.
english: Like never before, we are called to join hands and develop our nation by continuing the implementation of the bold initiatives to achieve development for all.

twi: Anyɛ bie koraa no, yɛahyɛ bo wo Ɔman Bɔhyhensem no mu sɛ yɛde yɛn ahoɔden ne yɛn akoma nyinaa bɛyɛ Ghana adwuma.
english: After all, we pledged ourselves to the service of Ghana with all our strength and with all our heart.

twi: Onyankopɔn nhyira yɛn nyinaa.
english: May God bless us all.

twi: 1. 2021 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehysee yi yɛ dwumadie a Aban dii no ne sika dodos a Aban de asi n'ani so sɛ ɔbɛnya de atu ne nhyehysee ne dwumadie ahodoɔ ho anammɔn wo 2021 mu no nyinaa ho tofabo. Asɛntire a ɛda saa Sikasɛm Nhyehysee yi so ne sɛ “Yebewie dwumadie ama asees atim na yzatoa des aka so nam so akanyan ɔman sikasem”.
english: 1 | Government of Ghana - 2021 Citizens’ Budget INTRODUCTION The 2021 Citizen’s Budget is a summary of what Government achieved in 2020 and how much it’s intends to collect in revenues to implement policies and programmes in 2021. The theme of the 2021 Budget is “Completion, Consolidation, and Continuation”.

twi: Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi kuta saa Asɛntire yi ɛsiane sɛ mmerɛ dodos a atwam no, na afe biara mu Sikasɛm nhyehysese wo dwumadie afoforɔ bebree a Aban pɛ sɛ ɔtu ho anammon, wo ɛberɛ a dwumadie a rekɔ so bebree wɔ ho a ɛho dwumadie nwiee peys.
english: This theme is underpinned by the fact that over the years every new Budget invariably contains a host of new projects to be initiated at the expense of ongoing projects.

twi: Ɛba saa a, ɛnyɛ yɛn Sikasɛm nko ara na ɛtɔ ape, na mmom ɛka bebree beda yɛn so a Ebi mpo wo hɔ a, yentumi ntua akontratafoo a wɔayɛ wɔn adwuma awie no ntɛm so.
english: Not only does this put pressure on our finances, but has also historically resulted in payments arrears, with many contractors not being paid on time for work done.

twi: Yei ma dwumadie ahodovs ho ska no ko soro dodo ɛsiane sɛ yɛtua nsiho wo dwumadie biara a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛtua ho ɛka a yɛatu ahyɛ ɛda no ho.
english: This raises the overall cost of projects as the deferred payments attract interest cost.

twi: Afe 2021 yi mu no, Aban asi gyinaeɛ sɛ ɔbetwa sa foforɔ ato ho.
english: In 2021, Government plans to chart a new direction.

twi: Saa ɛkwan foforɔ a Aban pɛ sɛ ɔfa so no botaeɛ ne se, ɔde tebea bi a akoye sɛ Amammerɛ bi a yehye dwumadie biara ase a na ysagyae ama aka nsensen mu no bsba awiees, ne saa enti, Aban asi nkete sɛ ɔbewie dwumadie ahodov a yenwiee no nyinaa.
english: The goal is to bring to an end the culture of unfinished projects by fulfilling commitments to complete existing projects.

english: Budget deficit: This occurs when Government expenditure is more than the revenue it mobilises.

english: Capital Expenditure: This is money spent on major infrastructure projects such as roads, schools, hospitals, bridges, transport, water systems, plant and machinery.

english: Compensation of Employees: This is made up of wages & salaries and salary-related allowances such as social security, gratuities and pensions paid to public sector workers.

twi: Mpontuo mu Aboafoɔ (Development Partners): Yei gyina ho ma Aman anaa nnwumakuo a woɔboa Aman a afei na woɔretu mpɔn ma wɔduru wɔn mpontuo botaes ho.

EƐtumi nso yɛ ankorankorɛ aman bi te sɛ Germany, Nyiresi Aburokyire, Amerika, ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
english: DPs can be multilateral, e.g. International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank, and African Development Bank (AfDB), or bilateral which consists of individual countries like Germany, United Kingdom, and the United States of America (USA).

english: End-Year Inflation: The level of inflation experienced in December of the year in consideration.
